high-voltage 6 kV class 4H-SIC rectifier diodes can withstand a current surge pulse with a duration of 8 ms and a current density of j ~ 7000 A cm− 2, which corresponds to the maximum temperature of the diode base equal to 1000 K.

4H-Silicon Carbide (SiC) p+–n-n+ rectifier diode structures are able to withstand current surge pulses of a single 1000 A cm−1 duration and a duration of 1000 A/cm2, even though the base temperature of the diode at the end of this pulse can be as high as 1100 K and the diode base can lose thermal stability.
the high-temperature thermal instability of the 4H-Sic diodes is a very serious problem, which must be taken into account in the design of power electronics.
